Then: 'Based upon information and belief, Defendants are further in breach of the Grant Agreement for failing to perform their Metric Commitments.' No job, payroll or investment figure is alleged. Note the two-grantee wording: breach is defined as to 'Grantees' collectively and the remedy runs against both, but the performance duty and the repayment duty are written against 'Grantee 1' only.

outcome: Voluntarily dismissed by JobsOhio without prejudice, after service failed twice. Filed 2023-10-26. Certified mail came back undelivered on 2024-02-06 and again on 2024-03-08; a change of address was filed on 2024-02-15. Neither defendant was ever served or appeared. On 2024-08-07 JobsOhio filed a 'Notice of Dismissal Without Prejudice': 'Now comes Plaintiff JobsOhio and hereby dismisses this action without prejudice.' The case terminated the same day.
amount_recovered: No filing states any amount. No judgment, no satisfaction. The defendants were never served, so the case never reached the merits.

notes: Two things stand out. First, the grant agreement has two grantees, an operating company and a related property company at the same address, with the metric and repayment duties written against the operating company but the breach definition and remedies reaching both. That is a second example in this batch of JobsOhio widening who can be made to repay, alongside the parent-company unjust enrichment claim in the Recleim case. Second, only $16,724 of a $75,000 authorization was ever drawn, which is a reminder that reimbursement-basis grants often pay out far less than the headline figure. The case died on failed service, not on the merits.

notes: Two findings worth carrying. First, the grantee can change: JobsOhio signed with Precision Tower Products LLC in 2014 and in 2016 substituted Sky Climber Fabricating, LLC into the same agreement, which is why a Form 990 grant schedule and a lawsuit caption can carry different names for the same money. Second, the court's 2021-08-25 decision denying JobsOhio's motion to strike records the company's complaint about JobsOhio's posture. The judge wrote that the defendant's filing 'actually reveals is a lack of settlement discussions in this matter. Specifically, it contends that it has reached out to plaintiff's counsel to discuss a protentional resolution, but the plaintiff has refused to negotiate.' (The typo is in the original.) Seven months later JobsOhio settled anyway. This is the only case in the batch where a judge wrote anything about how JobsOhio conducts these collections.
